Company overview · July 2026
Private & confidential
Firm, near-term power, extracted from existing grid infrastructure.
In brief
Neura Energy converts flexible and constrained grid connections into bankable, firm power for large industrial loads.
A battery-enabled firming service bridges existing low-utilisation infrastructure and bankable power provision.
IThe constraint

Grids are massively constrained and struggling to meet new demand, especially from High-Performance Computing (HPC). Global data-centre electricity consumption is projected to more than double by 2030.1 Power, not energy, is the overarching system constraint. Available interconnections are scarce, and waves of distributed energy deployments have occupied network operators and policymakers, leaving little recourse for further build-out in response to new demand. In an already slow-moving sector, this dynamic has left the system desperately behind as a new wave of energy-intensive technologies tries to energise. AI and robotics may be the largest industrial waves of our generation, but unless they can solve power-access issues, they will either need to hitch a ride to space or forgo potential growth.

IIThe opportunity

Power systems are engineered around their highest peaks. Average utilisation rates are around half of capability,2 with some networks seeing as little as 30% utilisation.3 Research suggests over 126 GW of new load could be connected in the US if it were curtailable for just 1% of its hours, in events averaging around two hours.4 Increasingly, regulators in the US and UK are acting to ensure network operators offer faster access to the grid, with ‘energy-only’ (non-firm) connection contracts increasingly promoted.

Currently, these connections are tough to underwrite. They are not bankable enough to secure the finance needed to build and energise, especially for high-uptime loads such as HPC, where financing is typically contingent on ‘5-nine’ power availability contracts. Recent deals have demonstrated that a real opportunity is emerging to repurpose, firm and underwrite existing grid connections for alternative uses.5 Early examples include bitcoin miners, where connection agreements typically already permit import. We believe opportunity exists for similar arrangements at a large number of existing grid connections, unlocked by detailed network modelling and custom, optimised storage systems designed to systematically and reliably cover shortfalls.

The shape of the opportunity

The product
A battery-enabled firming service.
IIIWhat Neura sells

Neura sells access to power. It profits from the difference in value between an existing, constrained grid connection and a version modified specifically for power provisioning, taking account of site-specific network and generation variables. This value can be captured by Neura either as a service provider to the connection owner, in which case the owner finances the incremental conversion capex, or directly, through lease agreements signed with connection owners. The latter approach would require a platform partner as a lease backstop, similar to the role Google played in the FluidStack deal.

Neura leases the right to flexible import capacity secured on accelerated timelines; finances and installs behind-the-meter battery storage sized to the curtailment duty; and implements battery and cooling controls that give the network operator and offtaker verifiable compliance.

How the battery firms the connection
IVSizing & service levels

Various battery power and duration combinations can be used to engineer required uptime against a given load curve. Additionally, alternative revenues in the form of capacity market participation and energy trading, in day-ahead and near-real-time balancing markets, can be considered. This underwriting is Neura’s current expertise — the power-provisioning focus is something we’re now leaning towards based on market feedback. Sizing is derived per site from modelling built on the network’s own constraint data. This output is verified by the Power System Architecture Lab at the University of Oxford, our consortium partner for the upcoming Innovate UK consumer-flexibility project, where we are looking to pilot this system.

Time to power
Indicative development timelines for large-load grid access; Neura’s firming layer makes the accelerated route contractible as firm power.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager

for f in ["/root/.fonts/Inter-Regular.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Medium.otf",
          "/root/.fonts/Inter-SemiBold.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Italic.otf"]:
    font_manager.fontManager.addfont(f)
matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"] = "Inter"
matplotlib.rcParams["svg.fonttype"] = "none"
matplotlib.rcParams["hatch.linewidth"] = 0.5

INK = "#141414"; GREY = "#6B6862"; FAINT = "#C9C5BD"
FILL = "#ECE9E2"; HATCH_C = "#E3C4A6"

x = np.linspace(0, 100, 4001)

def smoothstep(u, u0, u1):
    s = np.clip((u - u0) / (u1 - u0), 0, 1)
    return s * s * (3 - 2 * s)

fig, (a, b) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.85, 1.58),
                           gridspec_kw=dict(left=0.075, right=0.988,
                                            top=0.955, bottom=0.24,
                                            wspace=0.17))

def style(ax):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 100); ax.set_ylim(0, 104)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ["left", "bottom"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(0.6); ax.spines[s].set_color(INK)
    ax.tick_params(width=0.6, color=INK, labelsize=6.2, labelcolor=GREY,
                   length=2.2)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 25, 50, 75, 100])
    ax.set_xticklabels(["0", "25", "50", "75", "100%"])

# ------- (a) system LDC, sharp peak, ERCOT 2024 anchors ------------------
ya = 43 + 34 * (1 - x / 100) ** 0.9 + 23 * np.exp(-x / 2.1)
style(a)
a.set_yticks([0, 50, 100]); a.set_yticklabels(["0", "50", "100%"])
a.fill_between(x, ya, 100, facecolor="none", edgecolor=HATCH_C, hatch="///",
               lw=0, zorder=1)
a.fill_between(x, 0, ya, color=FILL, lw=0, zorder=2)
a.plot(x, ya, color=INK, lw=1.3, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=3)

a.text(45, 26, "System demand", fontsize=7.0, color=INK, weight="medium",
       ha="center")
a.text(55, 80, "Available capacity", fontsize=7.0, color="#A8713F",
       weight="medium", ha="center", zorder=5,
       bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=1.6))

a.set_ylabel("% of system peak", fontsize=6.3, color=INK, labelpad=4)
a.set_xlabel("(a)  Representative network utilisation \u2014 load duration curve",
             fontsize=6.5, color=GREY, labelpad=4.5)

# ------- (b) a battery site's grid connection: import duration curve -----
# 2 h system, ~1 cycle/day, import only -> connection used ~8.3% of hours
yb = (100 - 0.45 * x) * (1 - smoothstep(x, 6.0, 10.6))

style(b)
b.set_yticks([0, 50, 100]); b.set_yticklabels(["0", "50", "100%"])
b.set_xticks([0, 8.3, 25, 50, 75, 100])
b.set_xticklabels(["0", "8.3%", "25", "50", "75", "100%"])
b.fill_between(x, yb, 100, facecolor="none", edgecolor=HATCH_C, hatch="///",
               lw=0, zorder=1)
b.fill_between(x, 0, yb, color=FILL, lw=0, zorder=2)
b.plot(x, yb, color=INK, lw=1.3, solid_capstyle="round",
       solid_joinstyle="round", zorder=3)

b.plot([12.6, 6.0], [47, 51], color=GREY, lw=0.5, zorder=4)
b.text(13.6, 47, "Battery import \u2014 \u2248 8% of hours\nstandard 2 h utility-scale battery, ~1 cycle per day",
       fontsize=6.5, color=INK, ha="left", va="center", weight="medium",

       bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=1.8))
b.text(58, 78, "Available capacity", fontsize=7.0, color="#A8713F",

b.set_ylabel("% of connection used", fontsize=6.3, color=INK, labelpad=4)
b.set_xlabel("(b)  Battery grid import \u2014 load duration curve",
             fontsize=6.5, color=GREY, labelpad=4.5)

fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/ldc2.svg", format="svg")
fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/ldc2_preview.png", dpi=180)
lf = np.trapezoid(ya, x) / 100 / 100
print(f"panel a load factor {lf:.2f}, y(1%)={43+34*0.99**0.9+23*np.exp(-1/2.1):.0f}")
chart16.py
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d

for f in ["/root/.fonts/Inter-Regular.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Medium.otf",
          "/root/.fonts/Inter-SemiBold.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Italic.otf"]:
    font_manager.fontManager.addfont(f)
matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"] = "Inter"
matplotlib.rcParams["svg.fonttype"] = "none"

INK = "#141414"; GREY = "#6B6862"; DARKGREY = "#3D3B37"
ORANGE = "#E86A2B"
GRID_FILL = "#EAE7E0"
RECHG_FILL = "#F3DECB"
DASH = "#9A968E"

t = np.linspace(0, 24, 24 * 60 + 1)
dt = t[1] - t[0]
CONN = 100.0; FIRM_N = 78.0; FIRM_0 = 30.0; FLOOR = 25.0
DEPTH = 30.0

def ramp(x, x0, x1):
    s = np.clip((x - x0) / (x1 - x0), 0, 1)
    return s * s * (3 - 2 * s)

avail = np.full_like(t, CONN)
avail -= 8 * np.exp(-((t - 13.0) / 2.8) ** 2)
avail -= (CONN - DEPTH) * (ramp(t, 16.95, 17.35) - ramp(t, 18.98, 19.43))
avail = np.clip(avail, DEPTH, CONN)

imp = np.minimum(avail, FIRM_N)
r_m = 15.5 * (ramp(t, 0.8, 1.6) - ramp(t, 5.3, 6.3))
r_e = 15.5 * (ramp(t, 20.55, 21.35) - ramp(t, 23.8, 24.8))
imp = np.minimum(avail, imp + np.maximum(r_m, 0) + np.maximum(r_e, 0))

batt = FIRM_N - imp
d_energy = batt[batt > 0].sum() * dt
E = 136.0
soc = np.zeros_like(t); soc[0] = 61.0
for i in range(1, len(t)):
    soc[i] = min(100.0, soc[i - 1] - batt[i] * dt / E * 100)
soc = gaussian_filter1d(soc, sigma=9)

fig, (ax, axs) = plt.subplots(
    2, 1, figsize=(6.85, 2.62), sharex=True,
    gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[2.45, 1.05], hspace=0.20,
                     left=0.088, right=0.842, top=0.97, bottom=0.085))

# ---- main panel ---------------------------------------------------------
ax.set_xlim(0, 24); ax.set_ylim(0, 104)
for s in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
for s in ["left", "bottom"]:
    ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(0.6); ax.spines[s].set_color(INK)
ax.tick_params(width=0.6, color=INK, labelsize=6.4, labelcolor=GREY, length=2.2)
ax.set_yticks([0, 30, 78, 100]); ax.set_yticklabels(["0", "30", "78", "100%"])
ax.tick_params(labelbottom=False, bottom=False)
ax.set_ylabel("Grid connection capacity", fontsize=6.8, color=INK, labelpad=6)

ax.fill_between(t, 0, np.minimum(imp, FIRM_N), color=GRID_FILL, lw=0, zorder=2)
ax.fill_between(t, imp, FIRM_N, where=imp < FIRM_N - 0.05, color=ORANGE,
                lw=0, zorder=3)
ax.fill_between(t, FIRM_N, imp, where=imp > FIRM_N + 0.05, color=RECHG_FILL,
                lw=0, zorder=3)

ax.plot(t, avail, color=INK, lw=1.4, solid_capstyle="round",
        solid_joinstyle="round", zorder=6)
ax.plot([0, 24], [FIRM_N, FIRM_N], color=ORANGE, lw=1.6, zorder=5)
ax.plot([0, 24], [FIRM_0, FIRM_0], color=DASH, lw=0.9, ls=(0, (5, 3)),
        zorder=5)

ax.text(24.45, 100, "Available import\ncapacity", fontsize=6.4, color=GREY,
        va="center", ha="left", linespacing=1.45, clip_on=False)
ax.text(24.45, FIRM_N, "Firm potential\nwith Neura (78%)", fontsize=6.6,
        color=ORANGE, va="center", ha="left", weight="semibold",
        linespacing=1.45, clip_on=False)
ax.text(24.45, FIRM_0, "Firm potential\nwithout Neura (30%)",
        fontsize=6.6, color=DARKGREY, va="center", ha="left",
        linespacing=1.45, clip_on=False)

ax.text(8.6, 40, "From the grid", fontsize=7.2, color=INK, weight="medium",
        ha="center")
ax.text(18.2, 52, "From the\nbattery", fontsize=6.6, color="#FFFFFF",
        weight="semibold", ha="center", va="center", linespacing=1.45)
ax.text(3.35, 82.5, "Recharge", fontsize=6.0, color=GREY, ha="center",
        va="bottom")
ax.text(22.6, 82.5, "Recharge", fontsize=6.0, color=GREY, ha="center",
        va="bottom")

# ---- SOC panel ----------------------------------------------------------
axs.set_ylim(0, 110); axs.set_xlim(0, 24)
for s in ["top", "right"]:
    axs.spines[s].set_visible(False)
for s in ["left", "bottom"]:
    axs.spines[s].set_linewidth(0.6); axs.spines[s].set_color(INK)
axs.tick_params(width=0.6, color=INK, labelsize=6.4, labelcolor=GREY,
                length=2.2)
axs.plot(t, soc, color=ORANGE, lw=1.5, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=4)
axs.plot([0, 24], [FLOOR, FLOOR], color=DASH, lw=0.9, ls=(0, (5, 3)),
         zorder=3)
axs.set_yticks([0, 25, 100]); axs.set_yticklabels(["0", "25", "100%"])
axs.set_xticks(range(0, 25, 4))
axs.set_xticklabels([f"{h:02d}:00" for h in range(0, 25, 4)])
axs.set_ylabel("Battery SOC", fontsize=6.8, color=INK, labelpad=6)
axs.text(24.45, FLOOR, "Minimum\nreserve", fontsize=6.3, color=DARKGREY,
         ha="left", va="center", linespacing=1.45, clip_on=False)

fig.align_ylabels([ax, axs])
fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/day.svg", format="svg")
fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/day_preview.png", dpi=180)
print(f"discharge {d_energy:.0f}/96 | soc {soc[0]:.0f}->{soc.min():.0f}->{soc[-1]:.0f}")

FILL = "#DDD9D0"; ORANGE = "#E86A2B"; ORANGE_LT = "#F2A15F"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.85, 0.92))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.305, right=0.985, top=0.92, bottom=0.30)

ax.set_xlim(0, 7); ax.set_ylim(-0.65, 1.65)
for s in ["top", "right", "left"]:
    ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_linewidth(0.6); ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(INK)

        ha="right", va="center")
ax.text(6.05, 1, "5\u20137 years", fontsize=6.8, color=GREY, ha="left",
        va="center", weight="medium")

# Neura: flexible + firming

import numpy as np
import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager

for f in ["/root/.fonts/Inter-Regular.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Medium.otf",
          "/root/.fonts/Inter-SemiBold.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Italic.otf"]:
    font_manager.fontManager.addfont(f)
matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"] = "Inter"
matplotlib.rcParams["svg.fonttype"] = "none"
matplotlib.rcParams["hatch.linewidth"] = 0.5

INK = "#141414"; GREY = "#6B6862"; FAINT = "#C9C5BD"
FILL = "#ECE9E2"; HATCH_C = "#E3C4A6"

x = np.linspace(0, 100, 4001)

def smoothstep(u, u0, u1):
    s = np.clip((u - u0) / (u1 - u0), 0, 1)
    return s * s * (3 - 2 * s)

def style(ax):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 100); ax.set_ylim(0, 104)
    for s in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ["left", "bottom"]:
        ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(0.6); ax.spines[s].set_color(INK)
    ax.tick_params(width=0.6, color=INK, labelsize=6.4, labelcolor=GREY,
                   length=2.2)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 25, 50, 75, 100])
    ax.set_xticklabels(["0", "25", "50", "75", "100%"])

# ---------------- panel (a): network -------------------------------------
fig, a = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 1.95))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.095, right=0.985, top=0.95, bottom=0.225)
ya = 43 + 34 * (1 - x / 100) ** 0.9 + 23 * np.exp(-x / 2.1)
style(a)
a.set_yticks([0, 50, 100]); a.set_yticklabels(["0", "50", "100%"])
a.fill_between(x, ya, 100, facecolor="none", edgecolor=HATCH_C, hatch="///",
               lw=0, zorder=1)
a.fill_between(x, 0, ya, color=FILL, lw=0, zorder=2)
a.plot(x, ya, color=INK, lw=1.3, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=3)
a.text(45, 26, "System demand", fontsize=7.0, color=INK, weight="medium",
       ha="center")
a.text(55, 78, "Available capacity", fontsize=7.0, color="#A8713F",
       weight="medium", ha="center", zorder=5,
       bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=1.6))
a.set_ylabel("% of system peak", fontsize=6.4, color=INK, labelpad=4)
a.set_xlabel("(a)  Representative network utilisation \u2014 load duration curve",
             fontsize=6.6, color=GREY, labelpad=4.5)
fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/ldc_a_land.svg", format="svg")

# ---------------- panel (b): battery import ------------------------------
fig, b = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 1.95))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.095, right=0.985, top=0.95, bottom=0.225)
yb = (100 - 0.45 * x) * (1 - smoothstep(x, 6.0, 10.6))
style(b)
b.set_yticks([0, 50, 100]); b.set_yticklabels(["0", "50", "100%"])
b.set_xticks([0, 8.3, 25, 50, 75, 100])
b.set_xticklabels(["0", "8.3%", "25", "50", "75", "100%"])
b.fill_between(x, yb, 100, facecolor="none", edgecolor=HATCH_C, hatch="///",
               lw=0, zorder=1)
b.fill_between(x, 0, yb, color=FILL, lw=0, zorder=2)
b.plot(x, yb, color=INK, lw=1.3, solid_capstyle="round",
       solid_joinstyle="round", zorder=3)
b.plot([12.6, 6.0], [47, 51], color=GREY, lw=0.5, zorder=4)
b.text(13.6, 47, "Battery import \u2014 \u2248 8% of hours\nstandard 2 h utility-scale battery, ~1 cycle per day",
       fontsize=6.5, color=INK, ha="left", va="center", weight="medium",
       linespacing=1.55, zorder=5,
       bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=1.8))
b.text(58, 80, "Available capacity", fontsize=7.0, color="#A8713F",
       weight="medium", ha="center", zorder=5,
       bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", pad=1.6))
b.set_ylabel("% of connection used", fontsize=6.4, color=INK, labelpad=4)
b.set_xlabel("(b)  Battery grid import \u2014 load duration curve",
             fontsize=6.6, color=GREY, labelpad=4.5)
fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/ldc_b_land.svg", format="svg")
print("panels done")

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch

for f in ["/root/.fonts/Inter-Regular.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Medium.otf",
          "/root/.fonts/Inter-SemiBold.otf", "/root/.fonts/Inter-Italic.otf"]:
    font_manager.fontManager.addfont(f)
matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"] = "Inter"
matplotlib.rcParams["svg.fonttype"] = "none"

INK = "#141414"; GREY = "#6B6862"; DARKGREY = "#3D3B37"
ORANGE = "#E86A2B"; PANEL = "#FBF1E8"; FILL = "#F2F0EA"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 2.95))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.99, bottom=0.01)
ax.set_xlim(0, 100); ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.axis("off")

def box(x, y, w, h, fc, ec, lw=0.8, ls="-", r=1.6):
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch(
        (x, y), w, h, boxstyle=f"round,pad=0,rounding_size={r}",
        facecolor=fc, edgecolor=ec, linewidth=lw, linestyle=ls, zorder=2))

def arrow(x, y0, y1):
    ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((x, y0), (x, y1),
        arrowstyle="-|>", mutation_scale=9, color=INK, lw=1.0, zorder=3))

# ---- top: the input asset ----
box(22, 82, 56, 14.5, "white", INK, lw=0.9, ls=(0, (4, 2.4)))
ax.text(50, 91.7, "Constrained grid connection", fontsize=7.6, color=INK,
        ha="center", va="center", weight="semibold")
ax.text(50, 86.2, "existing site \u00b7 flexible or non-firm import",
        fontsize=6.2, color=GREY, ha="center", va="center")

arrow(50, 81, 74.5)

# ---- middle: the Neura layer ----
box(6, 38, 88, 35, PANEL, ORANGE, lw=1.1)
ax.text(10, 68.5, "NEURA", fontsize=7.2, color=ORANGE, ha="left",
        va="center", weight="semibold")
ax.text(10, 64.2, "firming layer", fontsize=6.0, color="#A8713F",
        ha="left", va="center")

mod_y, mod_h, mod_w = 42.5, 17.5, 25.4
for i, (title, sub) in enumerate([
    ("Lease or service\nagreement", "two capture routes;\nplatform backstop"),
    ("Behind-the-meter\nbattery", "sized to the\ncurtailment duty"),
    ("Controls &\ncompliance", "verifiable to network\nand offtaker"),
]):
    mx = 9.5 + i * (mod_w + 2.6)
    box(mx, mod_y, mod_w, mod_h, "white", "#E3C0A0", lw=0.7)
    ax.text(mx + mod_w / 2, mod_y + mod_h - 4.4, title, fontsize=6.4,
            color=INK, ha="center", va="center", weight="semibold",
            linespacing=1.35)
    ax.text(mx + mod_w / 2, mod_y + 4.6, sub, fontsize=5.6, color=GREY,
            ha="center", va="center", linespacing=1.35)

ax.text(50, 63.8, "detailed network modelling \u00b7 sized from the network\u2019s own constraint data",
        fontsize=5.9, color=DARKGREY, ha="center", va="center")

arrow(50, 37, 30.5)

# ---- bottom: the output ----
box(22, 14, 56, 15, INK, INK)
ax.text(50, 24.2, "Firm, bankable power", fontsize=7.8, color="white",
        ha="center", va="center", weight="semibold")
ax.text(50, 18.6, "high-availability supply \u00b7 financeable offtake",
        fontsize=6.2, color="#D8D4CC", ha="center", va="center")

# ---- side annotations: capture routes ----
ax.text(3, 55.5, "Route 1 \u2014 service provider:\nconnection owner funds\nconversion capex",
        fontsize=5.6, color=GREY, ha="left", va="center", linespacing=1.4,
        rotation=90)
ax.text(97, 55.5, "Route 2 \u2014 direct lease:\nNeura finances, platform\npartner backstops",
        fontsize=5.6, color=GREY, ha="right", va="center", linespacing=1.4,
        rotation=270)

fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/flow.svg", format="svg")
fig.savefig("/home/claude/neura/flow_preview.png", dpi=180)
